# Expert Review Brief — AI Rack Deployment Evidence (IDE-014)

This brief invites specialists in data-centre electrical, mechanical, network and operations engineering to review one bounded question each, using public material only. It accompanies `AI_RACK_DEPLOYMENT_VERIFICATION_DOSSIER_014.md`, an AI-assisted research candidate that no person has reviewed.

## Terms

- Participation is voluntary and unpaid. There is no deadline and no obligation to answer every question.
- You may review a single question. Disagreement, criticism and "this cannot be settled from public material" are all useful answers.
- Use only public, non-confidential material. Please do not share site records, contracts or anything under NDA.
- You will be named only if you give explicit permission, and only in the form you approve.
- A response is recorded as a specialist's comment on the question it answers. It is not represented as validation, certification or approval of the dossier, and AI-assisted analysis is never presented as independent human review.

## Questions

### 1. What load and failover tests should a commissioning record for a GB200 NVL72 rack power path contain to show the stated redundancy?

- **Domain:** Electrical infrastructure.
- **Why it matters:** Redundancy figures conflict in public sources, so only a test record can show what a site has.
- **What would settle it:** A test outline that a commissioning record can be checked against.
- **Public materials:** NVIDIA, “NVIDIA DGX GB Rack Scale Systems User Guide”, https://docs.nvidia.com/dgx/dgxgb200-user-guide/dgxgb200-user-guide.pdf; NVIDIA, “NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD: Next Generation Scalable Infrastructure for AI Leadership — Reference Architecture Featuring NVIDIA DGX GB200”, https://docs.nvidia.com/dgx-superpod/reference-architecture-scalable-infrastructure-gb200/latest/_downloads/238ab33ee345a7241fc2f15eedc2ff6c/RA11338001-DSPGB200-ReferenceArch.pdf

### 2. Without a published coolant specification, what must a liquid-loop commissioning record state for it to show the rack's cooling interface was met?

- **Domain:** Thermal and liquid cooling.
- **Why it matters:** The thermal domain has no public criterion to commission against.
- **What would settle it:** A minimum set of loop parameters and test conditions.
- **Public materials:** NVIDIA, “NVIDIA DGX GB Rack Scale Systems User Guide”, https://docs.nvidia.com/dgx/dgxgb200-user-guide/dgxgb200-user-guide.pdf; Open Compute Project, “Liquid to Liquid CDU Test Methodology and Performance Rating, Revision 1.0”, https://www.opencompute.org/documents/ocp-wp-l-lcdu-test-methodology-performance-rating-r1-pdf/

### 3. Which entries in an NVLink bring-up log show that the domain was configured as NVIDIA's sequence requires?

- **Domain:** Networking and interconnect.
- **Why it matters:** Bring-up is where power, cooling, firmware and network evidence meet.
- **What would settle it:** The log fields a reviewer should look for.
- **Public materials:** NVIDIA, “NVIDIA Mission Control Management Plane and Rack Setup with NVIDIA DGX GB200/GB300 NVL72 Systems Installation Guide (version 2.5.0)”, https://docs.nvidia.com/mission-control/docs/rack-bring-up-install/2.5.0/index.html

### 4. How should a reviewer judge whether a rack's firmware and software inventory is a consistent set when NVIDIA does not publish one?

- **Domain:** Firmware and software.
- **Why it matters:** A version inventory shows what is installed, not whether it is compatible.
- **What would settle it:** A method for checking consistency against NVIDIA's own documents.
- **Public materials:** NVIDIA, “NVIDIA Mission Control Software with NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 Systems Administration Guide”, https://docs.nvidia.com/pdf/nvidia-mission-control-software-with-nvidia-gb200-nvl72-systems-administration-guide.pdf; NVIDIA, “NVIDIA Mission Control Management Plane and Rack Setup with NVIDIA DGX GB200/GB300 NVL72 Systems Installation Guide (version 2.5.0)”, https://docs.nvidia.com/mission-control/docs/rack-bring-up-install/2.5.0/index.html

### 5. What observation period and measurements would make an operational monitoring record for an AI rack meaningful?

- **Domain:** Facility operations and monitoring.
- **Why it matters:** Operational observation is the last state and the one most often claimed without records.
- **What would settle it:** A minimum period and measurement set, with the reasoning.
- **Public materials:** NVIDIA, “NVIDIA Mission Control Software with NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 Systems Administration Guide”, https://docs.nvidia.com/pdf/nvidia-mission-control-software-with-nvidia-gb200-nvl72-systems-administration-guide.pdf
